thread:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-06-17 created by paging policy (latency spike > 3s for /v1/generate)

Sam K: Paging - high tail latency on hosted inference endpoints in us-west-2. Automated alerts started at ~18:20 UTC.

Jorge S: I'm on it. Reproducing now, looks like queuing/backpressure on the batching service.

Mei L: Tagging @Priya R and @Elena (Comms) — potential customer-visible impact, need status page + customer note.

Priya R: ETA for first public note? We should avoid premature wording. Start with "investigating" and region list.

Elena (Comms): Drafting. Proposal: "We are investigating degraded latency for Redwood hosted inference in us-west-2. Some requests may experience delays; engineers are actively mitigating." Keep it short.

Sam K: Agree. Add: "No evidence of data exfiltration; no errors returned aside from timeouts."

Alex (Legal): +1 on the safety line. Don't say "no data loss" until confirmed. Use "no indication of data exposure at this time."

Jorge S: Quick tech note for the status page: root cause suspected to be a failing autoscaler loop triggering many small GPU pods -> high scheduling churn -> batch queues growing. Working plan: 1) pause autoscale, 2) drain a subset of pods, 3) scale up warm pool.

Mei L: Can ops run the pause now?

Sam K: Running command: ```redwood infra autoscale pause --region us-west-2 --reason 'incident 1862501234'```

ops-bot: Command queued: autoscale pause (request id x9f3).

Jorge S: Pause applied. Draining 3 nodes now. Logs: ```[2026-03-06T18:26:11Z] pod/serve-gt-45 evicted, queue-length=312 -> 48``` Seeing immediate reduction in queue on that shard.

Sam K: Latency tail down to ~700ms on most pods. Still >2s for a small fraction.

Elena (Comms): Drafting customer notification for status.redwood.com and email: "We are investigating degraded latency affecting inference requests in us-west-2. Mitigation actions underway; users may see intermittent slow responses. We will post updates every 30 minutes or as there are material changes." Anything to add?

Priya R: Add guidance for customers: if they have critical SLAs, suggest switching routing to us-east-1 as a temporary workaround, include snippet for SDK override.

Elena (Comms): Adding code snippet: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(region='us-east-1')
# override endpoint to route away from us-west-2
```

Alex (Legal): Approve present wording. No promises about SLA credits in the public note; route that through CS separately.

Jorge S: Recommend internal severity note: Sev-2 -> start customer outreach to top 10 affected tenants after next update.

Mei L: Who on CS will do outreach? cc: @Priya R will coordinate.

Priya R: I'll ping CS and Solutions. Draft email for affected customers: short summary, ETA for full mitigation (~30-60m), workaround (route), contact for urgent escalations, link to status page.

Elena (Comms): Social / public messaging: We should not post a tweet unless the service reaches wider visibility on status page and CS outreach is underway. If we do, tone should be: factual, non-alarming, link to status page. Draft tweet: "We're investigating increased latency for inference requests in us-west-2. Engineers are mitigating; some requests may be slower. See status.redwood.com for updates." Thoughts?

Sam K: Fine, but add "workaround: set region override" only in the status page / customer email, not in the tweet.

Alex (Legal): Suggest adding "No indication of data exposure" in the status page copy per above.

Elena (Comms): Final status page copy ready for posting (30m cadence). Will include pinned update + timeline. I'll put the first public post at 18:35 UTC.

ops-bot: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-03-06-17 (update_id=1)

Priya R: CS outreach in flight. Sending targeted emails to top affected customers now.

Jorge S: Working on post-mitigation test plan to validate long-tail requests under load. Will follow up on runbook changes to autoscaler thresholds.

Mei L: Once stability confirmed, we need a public follow-up message: cause summary, mitigation steps, and any customer actions. And internal RC (root-cause) doc.

Elena (Comms): For the public follow-up (tweet + blog short post) — draft: "Incident resolved: routing autoscaler churn caused increased latency in us-west-2. We paused autoscaling and drained affected pods; latency has returned to nominal. We're updating our autoscale thresholds to prevent recurrence. See full post: link" Keep blog post for details.

Alex (Legal): Approve follow-up phrasing. Make sure the blog post includes timeline and what we're changing.

Sam K: Confirming mitigation complete. Running extended synthetic test for 45m.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-06-17 status -> mitigated (18:52 UTC).

Mei L: Great. Elena, please coordinate final tweet + blog and get comms + legal sign-off; Priya please close the CS loop.

Elena (Comms): Will post tweet after legal sign-off. Draft tweet v2: "Mitigated: we resolved an incident affecting inference latency in us-west-2. No indication of data exposure. Full details: blog.redwood.com/incident-1862501234"

Alex (Legal): Approved.

Priya R: CS follow-ups sent. Notifying customer success manager for each tenant.

Sam K: I'll add a short note to the on-call runbook about autoscaler cooldowns and add an automated guard to halt rapid scale-up if eviction rate spikes.

Mei L: Thanks team. Closing incident thread once postmortem is published.

ops-bot: Incident closed (final) at 19:40 UTC. Postmortem link to be attached when available.
